paper_metadata.title: Quantum Generative Models of Mid-Price Movement in Limit Order Books

summary: The paper proposes and trains gate-based quantum hidden Markov models for limit order book mid-price movement, using AMZN and GOOGL event-time and 1-second aggregated data. It reports 3-qubit model order, 4-qubit hardware circuits, transpiled two-qubit depths of 53 and 86, and hardware histograms that match 3-symbol target distributions with variational distance below 1e-4 in the modeled cases.

experiments.description: Quantum generative model (QHMM/UQHMM) trained on AMZN and GOOGL limit order book mid-price movement sequences at event time and 1-second aggregation, evaluated by matching empirical sequence distributions and variational distance.

algorithm.variant: Unitary Quantum Hidden Markov Model (UQHMM) / quantum generative model with mid-circuit measurement
algorithm.optimizer: memetic algorithm with evolutionary global search + Metropolis annealing local search + non-linear parametric optimization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: maximum 300 evolutionary generations or until best fitness exceeds -1e-4
algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial population of 200 random hypotheses drawn uniformly from hypothesis space; initial state prepared as maximally mixed state

problem_formulation.encoding_details: binary mid-price movement y_t in {0,1} encoded as emission symbol; measurement qubit maps 0/1 via presence/absence of final X gate
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize negative empirical variational distance F(Q) = -Delta_{<=n}(D^L || D^Q) between target and model sequence distributions
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: none reported beyond unitary circuit structure and symbol-to-measurement map

problem_instance.description: Directional mid-price movement prediction/generation for limit order books using historical event-level and 1-second aggregated data
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: compute mid-price returns from LOB events; define directional movement y_t = 1 if return > 0 else 0; for 1-second aggregation use last mid-price in each interval
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: compare empirical and model sequence distributions; optimize variational distance to < 1e-4; evaluate Hankel rank estimates and low-rank approximation; hardware run compared target vs hardware histograms for 3-symbol sequences

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise; dynamical decoupling error suppression and Pauli twirling error mitigation

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Eagle r3 native gate set
implementation_details.classical_solver: non-linear solvers for parametric optimization; evolutionary algorithm on classical CPU
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Hankel rank estimation; low-rank approximation; empirical frequency estimation of sequence distributions
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compare model and target distributions; compute variational distance; histogram comparison of hardware output to target

speedup_claims.conditions: parsimony claim from QHMM literature; not an empirical runtime comparison in this paper
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states QHMMs can represent some stochastic process languages with sqrt(n) states compared with n-state classical HMMs; this is a theoretical representational-parsimony claim, not a measured speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: quadratically better parsimony than classical HMMs (as claimed via QHMM literature)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 3-qubit and 4-qubit gate-based QHMM circuits; transpiled depths 53 (AMZN) and 86 (GOOGL) for 3 time steps; IBM Eagle r3 QPU execution with error mitigation
limiting_factors: No classical runtime baseline is reported for the hardware experiment
Only small circuits on a 4-qubit layout are tested
Reported benefit is theoretical parsimony, not empirical speedup
Quadratic parsimony claim is insufficient under Hoefler constant-factor analysis
Circuit depth remains substantial after transpilation (53 and 86 two-qubit depth)

notes: num_qubits inferred from '3 qubits' model plus 1 emission/measurement qubit shown in 4-qubit circuits; paper explicitly states circuits are built for 4 qubits.
circuit_depth_transpiled values are paper-reported for 3 time steps: 53 and 86 after transpilation.

speedup_order set to quadratic based on paper's statement that QHMMs have quadratically better parsimony than classical counterparts; this is a theoretical parsimony claim, not an empirical runtime speedup.

The paper reports successful execution on IBM Eagle r3 QPU and good agreement between target and hardware histograms for 3-symbol sequences, but does not provide a classical baseline comparison for the hardware run.
The only advantage-like claim is theoretical parsimony of QHMMs over classical HMMs, not a demonstrated practical advantage.
